hints: The goal prioritizes the position of course 1, then course 2, and so on.
Construct the schedule backward, choosing a course with no unfinished successors.
Among those courses choose the largest label to place last.
analogy: Reserve the latest available slot for the largest course that no remaining course depends on.
example: With requirement 2 before 1 and independent 3, place 3 last, then 1, then 2, producing [2,1,3].
algorithm: Track each course's remaining outgoing edges and keep all zero-outdegree courses in a max-heap. Repeatedly remove the largest, append it to a reverse schedule, and decrease the outgoing counts of its predecessors. Reverse the resulting list.
correctness: A sink can always be placed last. Choosing the largest available sink leaves every smaller competing course earlier whenever possible; applying the same exchange argument recursively minimizes course positions in label order.
complexity: For n courses and m requirements, O((n+m) log n) time and O(n+m) space.
